research_question: In a university academic writing course, does a guardrailed AI writing assistant (feedback-only → AI-assisted revision with explanation) improve independent writing ability without increasing AI dependency, academic-integrity risk, or false confidence, compared to traditional no-AI writing instruction?

groups.treatment: one section using the 4-phase guardrailed AI writing-assistant policy
groups.comparison: one matched section without AI access (same instructor, materials and rubrics)

baseline: week-1 independent writing assessment in a strictly no-AI environment (writing quality rubric, fluency, grammar/accuracy)
post_test: week-8 independent writing assessment in a no-AI environment (same rubric as baseline)
retention_test: delayed writing task 4-6 weeks after the pilot ends, in a no-AI environment
transfer_test: week-8 novel academic writing task on an unseen topic in a strictly no-AI environment
process_metrics: AI usage logs: prompts submitted, feedback requested, accepted vs rejected suggestions
revision memo completeness and explanation quality
help-seeking behaviour: self-generated revision vs AI-suggested revision ratio
draft revision counts and writing fluency measures
learning_metrics: independent writing score on no-AI assessments (baseline / post / retention / transfer)
writing quality rubric (structure, argument, grammar, vocabulary)
retention on the delayed no-AI writing task
risk_metrics: ai_dependency: usage-without-understanding index from revision-memo quality and ratio of unexplained AI edits
academic_integrity_risk: detected copying of AI-generated text without attribution/explanation; integrity violations per submission
false_confidence: predicted grade vs actual grade gap on no-AI assessments; self-reported confidence vs independent performance
analysis_plan: Pre-registered comparison of treatment vs comparison sections on baseline-adjusted learning metrics (ANCOVA); learning metrics (no-AI independent writing) analysed separately from process/task metrics; subgroup analysis by initial writing proficiency; risk metrics monitored weekly with stop-condition checks at weeks 3, 5, 7 and at the transfer test.
success_threshold: treatment shows non-inferior independent writing (delta within 5%) AND equal or better retention AND AI dependency index and integrity violations below thresholds; if independent writing declines >10% on the transfer test, the pilot is judged unsuccessful regardless of in-class score gains.
stop_conditions: independent writing transfer-test decline >10% vs comparison
integrity violations (unexplained AI copying) in >20% of submissions
ai_dependency index exceeding the pre-set threshold for two consecutive weeks
false-confidence gap widening beyond the pre-set bound across two consecutive assessments
